evidence: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105 does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and then line 107 calls `tu.notification_level` with no nil guard. Nothing in the unsubscribe action creates a TopicUser row first: TopicView.new does not, and track_visit only happens in the show flow. So a logged-in user who opens /t/slug/id/unsubscribe for a topic they have no TopicUser row for gets a NoMethodError and a 500. That covers a forwarded email opened by another logged-in user, or a URL edited by hand. Fix: use TopicUser.change / find_or_initialize, or guard against nil.

app/models/topic.rb:719-721 builds unsubscribe_url as "#{url}/unsubscribe", and Topic#url (topic.rb:709-711) calls Topic.url (topic.rb:703-704), which builds "#{Discourse.base_url}/t/#{slug}/#{id}". The URL is therefore already absolute, unlike relative_url at line 713. user_notifications.rb:295 passes post.topic.unsubscribe_url, which is that absolute URL. The relative "/t/1234/unsubscribe" in spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb:172 is only test input.

The diff adds TopicsController#unsubscribe (topics_controller.rb:98-116), Topic#unsubscribe_url, and the routes in config/routes.rb:440-441. The only spec change is one extra option in spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb:171-172. spec/controllers/topics_controller_spec.rb has no unsubscribe tests at all (grep finds none), so none of these are covered: the login requirement (ensure_logged_in list at line 8-28), the slug-mismatch 301 redirect, the watching/tracking→regular and regular→muted transitions, or the missing-TopicUser case from issue 0, which is a real crash.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:7 ends with `}.property("model.fancyTitle"),` just before `})`. Trailing commas in object literals are valid since ES5. These .js.es6 files go through the ES6 transpiler, so older JS engines are not a concern. The same pattern already exists in controllers/user-topics-list.js.es6, so it does not break codebase convention either. A missing semicolon after `})` (line 9) is at most a cosmetic nit, and the reviewer did not raise it.

controllers/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:5 defines `stopNotificiationsText`, which really is misspelled (extra 'i'). It is cosmetic only: templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs:3 uses the same misspelled name, so the binding works and nothing is broken at runtime. Renaming improves readability; if you rename it, change the template too.

templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs:3 uses `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}`, which matches the controller property's current spelling, so it works as-is. This item only matters together with issue 4: the template has to be renamed at the same time as the controller or the binding breaks. On its own it is a cosmetic typo fix.
